logline: A museum curator who secretly obsesses over a K-pop idol fabricates a fake romance with her cold new boss - only for the pretense to become inconveniently real.

renewal.note: Single-season, 16-episode series that concluded on tvN on May 30, 2019. No continuation was announced.

bollymeter.basis: Park Min-young and Kim Jae-wook's on-screen chemistry is the engine that carries this fangirl rom-com well past its premise's ceiling. Reviewers praised their mature, communicative dynamic - unusual in K-drama - while noting the final stretch lost momentum. IMDb audience settled at 7.6.

pull_quotes.text: Park Min Young and Kim Jae Wook have wonderful chemistry that makes viewers swoon, laugh, cry, and cheer for them.

seasons.review_body: Her Private Life aired on tvN from April to May 2019, averaging 2.664% nationwide (AGB Nielsen) - modest by broadcast standards but solid for a cable romantic comedy. Park Min-young plays Sung Deok-mi, a composed museum curator with a secret: she is a hardcore fangirl of a K-pop idol. When her gallery hires Ryan Gold (Kim Jae-wook) as its new director, Deok-mi agrees to a fake relationship to deflect fan backlash. The conceit is lighter-than-air, and the show knows it. What earned critical affection was the maturity baked into the central relationship - misunderstandings get cleared through actual conversation rather than the usual K-drama stonewalling. Kim Jae-wook, primarily a character actor before this, proved himself a fully capable romantic lead. The Fangirl Verdict called it a show that understands its own genre completely. The show stumbles in its final four episodes, where the energy flags noticeably - a pattern reviewers cited consistently. For audiences who love the genre, the first twelve episodes deliver precisely what they promise.

episode_reviews.title: Do You Know What It Means To Be a Fan?
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere sets up the dual life of Deok-mi with zippy comic timing. Park Min-young calibrates the fangirl identity as something the character is neither ashamed of nor defined by - a smarter choice than the premise suggests.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The reveal of Deok-mi's elaborate fan shrine, reframing everything the audience assumed about her in the first act.
